commits.message: docs(markup-tags): raw content is still parsed, attribute values cannot hold brackets, theme names are not reserved (rich-docs-qi5)
docs(markup): a page for plugin tags — registering, the handler contract, which registry, and why pairs must nest (rich-docs-qi5)

fix(host): suspend stops the job, signals coexist with signal-exit, a program's end leaves run unsettled (rich-runtime-fna.3)

From the /code-review high pass on PR #198:

- NodeTerminalHost.suspend sends SIGTSTP to the process group, as the
  terminal sends Ctrl+Z, so a launcher (npm run, sh -c) stops with the
  program and the shell takes the terminal. A signal to one's own group is
  delivered inside kill, so suspend resolves when the call returns: no
  SIGCONT wait and no keep-alive timer, and a discarded SIGTSTP (no job
  control) no longer strands the app suspended.
- onExit's signal listeners are prepended, so a listener keeping the same
  raise-only-when-alone rule (signal-exit) finds itself alone and raises
  the signal instead of both standing down.
- When the program ends under the app, run() does not settle, so no code
  after it runs inside a crash's report and exit.
- An inline frame that blanks rows below it rewinds to its own height.
- installTraceback raises an unhandled rejection after its other listeners
  have heard it.
- rich-explore ends the app with a reducer's error again.

feat(host): App, the runtime that takes the terminal and hands it back on every exit (rich-runtime-fna.3)

App paints one renderable per frame on an alternate or inline surface,
repaints on refresh() and resize, suspends through the host, and undoes the
alternate screen, hidden cursor and raw mode on stop, a throwing frame, and
every way the program can end under it.

TerminalHost gains onExit and suspend. The node host hears exit, SIGINT,
SIGTERM, SIGHUP and uncaughtExceptionMonitor, keeps each ending's default
outcome, and suspends by SIGTSTP with a timer holding the loop until SIGCONT.

installTraceback now throws unhandled rejections into the uncaught channel,
so node's monitor phase restores the terminal before every report prints.

rich-explore runs on App, with Ctrl+Z to suspend.
fix(markup): halve the backslash run in front of a tag, as Rich does; escape inverts both parser rules (rich-markup-nm1) (#195)

fix(markup): an implicit close [/] closes a plugin tag, as it closes any other (rich-markup-gfr) (#196)

pairPluginTags kept a stack of plugin tags only, so it could not tell what [/]
referred to and skipped it: [shout]one[/] fell back to the built-in parser,
which dropped [shout] as an unknown style without a word. The pass now keeps
the built-in dialect's full stack, style tags included, and pairs a plugin tag
when [/] pops it. [/name] matching is one predicate shared by both walks.

fix(markup): a style tag spans a plugin pair it encloses (rich-markup-cg6)

The plugin-aware walk rendered the text between plugin pairs as separate
built-in parses, so every style tag closed at the first pair's boundary and
its closing tag then matched nothing: '[bold]x[click]y[/click]z[/bold]'
threw "doesn't match any open tag" with [bold] visibly open. Since gfr let
[/] close a plugin tag, '[bold][aa]x[/][/]' threw the same way, and an
unclosed '[bold]pre [aa]x[/aa] post' silently lost bold after the pair.

Each plugin pair's handler output now takes the pair's place in one built-in
walk over the slice, so an enclosing style covers it like plain text and the
handler's own spans repaint it as an inner tag would. The same change stops
a base style from painting over markup colours whenever a plugin pair is
present, which the final whole-output stylize used to do.

A style tag that opens on one side of a plugin pair's boundary and closes on
the other has no span to give, since the handler replaces the text inside;
the pairing walk now rejects it with an error naming the plugin boundary.
